- the **"Contact form pro"** block;
- the contact form that AI-generated sites always include;
- the editor's other native forms.

## Where to see submissions

Every submission is always saved, even if the email notification fails, and shows up under the **"Leads"** tab of "Project settings": "Messages from your published site's contact forms. Showing the 200 most recent." If you don't have any yet: "No form submissions yet…".

If you think a message isn't reaching you, check the "Leads" tab first: every submission is saved there, whether or not the email notification arrived.

## Anti-spam protection

Forms in the **"Contact form pro"** block and the ones in AI-generated sites have a honeypot field against bots and a limit of **10 submissions per minute**. You just need to fill in at least one of: name, email or message.

What your visitor sees after sending — these messages are fixed in Spanish regardless of the interface language: the Pro block shows an inline notice, "✓ Mensaje enviado. Te respondemos pronto."; AI-generated sites show a separate page titled "¡Gracias!" with "✓ Tu mensaje fue enviado. Te contactaremos pronto." and a "← Volver al sitio" link. If you leave all three fields empty: "Por favor completa al menos tu nombre o correo y un mensaje."

## If you export your site

If you download your site as a ZIP or export it via FTP, forms stop working outside Yammbo Web: the file carries an internal placeholder that only gets replaced with the real address when the site is served from `web.yammbo.com`. To keep receiving contact messages on an exported site, you'll need to hook up your own form service on your hosting.

## Next step

See how to export your site in [Export or download your site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/export-or-download-your-site/).

en.title: Manage your projects
en.description: The Yammbo Web Dashboard — open, preview, configure or delete a site — and what doesn't exist yet, like duplicating or renaming a project.
en.body:
## The Dashboard

At `/dashboard` you'll see the **"Dashboard"** title, a site counter, a **"Search sites..."** field and a sort order of "Date created", "Alphabetical" or "Last updated". Each card has an **"Open editor"** button.

If you haven't created any sites yet: "You have not created any sites yet".

## Each site's menu (⋮)

- **Edit** — opens the editor.
- **Preview** — opens the site in a new tab.
- **Settings** — publishing, forms, leads and export.
- **Delete** — asks you to confirm with "Are you sure you want to delete this project?"

Deleting a project removes its folder and its record entirely. There's no trash and no way to recover it afterwards.

## What doesn't exist yet

- **Duplicating an entire project.** You can only duplicate individual pages within the same site — see [Site pages](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/site-pages/).
- **Renaming a project or changing its URL** from the interface.
- **Sharing the project with someone else or inviting collaborators.**

## Next step

Review your account settings in [Your account](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/your-account/).

en.title: What is Yammbo Web
en.description: Visual website builder with templates, drag-and-drop blocks and AI. What it's for, what it doesn't include, and when to use Yammbo Store instead.
en.body:
Yammbo Web is Yammbo's website builder, at `web.yammbo.com`: a visual drag-and-drop editor, with ready-made templates and an AI that can generate your whole site from a description. It's built for **simple business sites** — landing pages, one-pagers, portfolios, the website of a restaurant, a clinic or a law firm — not for an online store with a cart, and not for a blog.

## What you can build

- One-page (landing) or multi-page sites.
- A site from scratch, from one of the 225 available templates, or generated by AI from a description of your business.
- Contact forms, galleries, hours, a WhatsApp button, maps and more, with the editor's blocks.

## What it does NOT include

- **It's not a store.** There's no cart, products or payments on the sites you build here. If you need to sell products online, Yammbo's product for that is **Yammbo Store**.
- **No blog**: there's no posts module or categories.
- **No free subdomain**: every site lives at `web.yammbo.com/sites/your-site` (see [Publish your site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/publish-your-site/)).
- **No HTML editor**: the custom code dialog only has CSS and JavaScript.
- **No domain registration or email hosting**: you can connect a domain you already own, but you can't buy one here (see [Custom domain](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/custom-domain/)).

## How a site gets built, in short

There are three paths: start blank, start from a template, or ask the AI to generate the whole site from a description of your business. All three end up in the same editor. Details for each are in [Create a site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/create-a-site/).

Generating a full site with AI, generating or editing sections with AI, and writing or rewriting text with AI are only available on the Basic, Standard and Pro plans. On the Free plan those buttons are locked. See [Plans and billing](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/plans-and-billing/).

## Next step

If you don't have an account yet, continue with [Create your account and sign in](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/create-your-account-and-sign-in/).

en.title: Plans and billing
en.description: Pricing for Free, Basic, Standard and Pro, what each plan includes, the real 1-published-site limit on every plan, and how to change or cancel your plan.
en.body:
## The plans

| Plan | Monthly | Annual | File space | AI site generations | AI text tokens per month | AI images per month | Custom domains | ZIP | FTP | Custom code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | 0 | — | 200 MB | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | No | No | No |
| **Basic** | $9 | $84 | 500 MB | 5/month | 300,000 | 2,000 | 1 | No | No | Yes |
| **Standard** ("Most popular") | $19 | $180 | 2 GB | 15/month | 900,000 | 6,000 | 1 | Yes | No | Yes |
| **Pro** | $39 | $372 | 10 GB | 40/month | 2,400,000 | 20,000 | 2 | Yes | Yes | Yes |

The annual plan saves 20–22% versus paying monthly; the pricing table shows this as "Save up to :percentage%".

No matter which plan you're on, you can only have **1 site published at the same time**. The number of projects (unpublished drafts) is unlimited on every plan. To publish another site, you first need to unpublish the one that's currently live — see [Publish your site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/publish-your-site/).

## What the Free plan actually gets you

On the Free plan you can't use any AI feature — AI buttons appear locked or open a notice that it's a paid-plan feature. The Free plan also has no custom code, ZIP, FTP or custom domain, and 200 MB of storage.

## How AI tokens are counted

Generating a full site, generating or editing a section, or writing or rewriting a piece of text all draw from the current month's text tokens. As a reference:

- a full site uses roughly **44,000 tokens** on average (anywhere from 17,900 to 137,900 depending on size);
- editing a section uses around 3,100;
- a new section uses around 1,350.

An AI-generated image counts as 1 "image token". Token and generation quotas reset on the 1st of each month. When your quota runs out you'll see: "You have used all the AI tokens included in your plan this month. They reset on the 1st, or you can upgrade for a larger allowance."

## Subscribing or changing plans

At `/pricing`, "Choose the right plan for you": a "Monthly" / "Annual" switch and **"Get started"** or **"Upgrade"** buttons. Payment is by card (Stripe) or PayPal. Checkout warns: "You'll be charged until you cancel your subscription. Previous charges won't be refunded when you cancel unless it's legally required…"

Once you have an active subscription, under **Billing** (your account menu):

- **Change plan**: "Available plans" → "Confirm your new plan" → "You will be charged the new price starting November 1, 2026".
- **Cancel plan**: "Your plan will be canceled, but is still available until the end of your billing period on November 1, 2026". You can undo this with "Renew plan" as long as the period hasn't ended.
- **Payment method**: "Change payment method".
- **Payment history**: a list of charges, marked Paid or Unpaid.

## Next step

With a plan picked, continue with [Create a site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/create-a-site/).

en.title: Preview, save and undo
en.description: How "Preview", "Save", "Undo"/"Redo", the History panel and "Design check" work in the Yammbo Web editor — and why it pays to save often.
en.body:
## Preview

The eye icon, in the bottom toolbar, opens your site (`/sites/{your-site}`) in a new tab. You can see it even if it isn't published yet, because you're the owner.

If you've made changes and haven't clicked "Save" yet, preview won't show them.

## Save

The **"Save"** button only becomes active when there are pending changes. Saving shows "Project saved", and your site's thumbnail on the Dashboard gets updated too.

Yammbo Web doesn't autosave, and it won't warn you if you close the editor with unsaved changes. The habit worth building: click "Save" every time you finish a meaningful change.

## Undo and redo

**"Undo"** and **"Redo"** buttons in the bottom toolbar, or the **Ctrl+Z** and **Ctrl+Y** shortcuts. They work on almost any action: inserting an element, changing a style, or even the result of "Edit section with AI".

## History

The **"History"** panel lists changes since you opened the site, for example "Inserted element", "Changed background" or "Edited section with AI". It's useful to understand what happened, not just to undo the last step.

## Design check

The **"Design check"** button analyses the page **at whichever screen size you're currently viewing** (mobile, tablet, small desktop or large desktop) and flags issues like overlapping elements, low contrast or overflowing content. It's free, runs in your browser, and doesn't depend on your plan.

- If it finds something: "Found 3 things worth looking at, at this screen size. Click one to jump to it." — clicking an issue selects the element.
- If it finds nothing: "No problems found at this screen size. Check the other sizes with the device selector."

## Next step

Once your site is ready, continue with [Publish your site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/publish-your-site/).

en.title: Publish your site
en.description: Publishing and unpublishing, the /sites/your-site URL, the 1-published-site-per-account limit, caching time, and the SEO that's applied automatically.
en.body:
Everything lives in **"Project settings"**, opened from the Dashboard (⋮ menu → "Settings") or from the editor ("Settings"), under the **"Publishing"** tab.

## Publishing and unpublishing

You'll see "Your site is published" or "Your site is not published", with a **"Publish"** or **"Unpublish"** button. Publishing shows "Project published"; unpublishing shows "Project unpublished".

If a visitor opens the URL of an unpublished site, they're redirected to the login page — nobody but you can see it.

If you already have a site published and try to publish another one, you'll see: "Has alcanzado el límite de sitios publicados de tu plan. Mejora tu plan para publicar más sitios." (shown in Spanish regardless of your interface language, since this message isn't translated). This applies even on the Pro plan. To publish a new site, unpublish the one that's currently live first.

## Your site's address

Your site lives at **`web.yammbo.com/sites/{your-site}`**, with no trailing slash — it shows up as "Preview url" under the "Publishing" tab. The slug comes from your project's name (for example, "Café Luna & Co." becomes `cafe-luna-co`) and **can't be changed from the interface**.

Your published site is cached with `max-age=60` and `stale-while-revalidate=60`, so if you saved a change and don't see it yet on the public URL, wait about 2 minutes and reload.

## Automatic SEO

Every published site ships, without any setup on your part, with `robots` tags, Open Graph (`og:type`, `og:title`, `og:url`), a Twitter Card and structured data (JSON-LD).

- **Per page**: under Pages → each page's Settings, you can set a custom Title, Description and Keywords.
- **"SEO config" block** (under Elements → Yammbo): title, description, keywords, a share image (Open Graph), canonical URL, robots, the structured-data type (page, organization, local business, person, service), your business name, phone and address, plus a Google Analytics ID and a Meta Pixel ID. This block doesn't show on the published site: it gets converted into `<head>` tags.
- **Sitemap**: available at `/sites/{your-site}/sitemap.xml` (or `/sitemap.xml` if you're using a custom domain).

The title search engines and social networks see (og:title) comes from the title you set in the **"SEO config"** block; if there isn't one, it falls back to your project's name (on the home page) or the page's name. The Title field under Pages → each page's Settings only changes the browser tab title, not the og:title.

## What doesn't exist in Yammbo Web

There are no free subdomains (like `your-name.yammbo.com`) and no configurable favicon — neither option appears in the interface.

## Next step

If you want to use a domain you already own, continue with [Custom domain](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/custom-domain/).

en.title: Site pages
en.description: Creating, duplicating, setting SEO for and deleting pages in Yammbo Web — what you can't delete and what each page's URL looks like.
en.body:
## Creating a page

In the **"Pages"** panel → **"New page"**: "Name", "Title", "Description" and "Keywords" ("Separate each keyword with a comma.").

## Editing, duplicating or deleting

Using the gear icon on each page:

- **Settings** — edit that page's SEO (title, description, keywords).
- **Duplicate** — creates a copy named `name-copy`.
- **Delete**.

Creating, duplicating or deleting a page **saves the project immediately**, without you needing to click "Save".

## What you can't do

- **You can't delete the `index` page**, nor the only page a site has if there's just one.
- If you reuse a page name: "A page with this name already exists."

## Each page's URL

Your published site's pages are served at `web.yammbo.com/sites/{your-site}/{page-name}`.

## Next step

If you're on a paid plan, give your blocks and sections a boost with [AI in the editor](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/ai-in-the-editor/).

en.title: Text, images and styles
en.description: How to edit text, upload or generate images, change icons and links, and what each section of the Yammbo Web Inspector does.
en.body:
## Editing text

**Double-click** any text to enter edit mode. Selecting a word or phrase brings up a floating toolbar with bold, underline, italic, link and insert icon.

## Uploading images

Double-click an image, or use the **"Upload image"** button in the Inspector. The file picker only accepts images.

- **Blocked file types** across the whole site: php, phtml, phar, cgi, pl, py, rb, sh, htaccess, jsp, asp(x), exe, so, and others. Message: "This file type is not allowed".
- **There's no per-file size limit** for images uploaded from the editor — only your **plan's total space** counts (200 MB, 500 MB, 2 GB or 10 GB). When it runs out: "You have exhausted your allowed space of 500 MB. Delete some files or upgrade your plan."
- Exception: the **logo** in the AI dialog goes through the server, and there the limit is **20 MB**.

If an image won't upload, it's most likely the file extension (check it isn't a blocked format) or that you've run out of plan storage.

## Icons

The **"Change icon"** button on an icon-type element, or the icon in the floating toolbar → "Select an icon" → "Search icons...".

## Links and buttons

The **"Change link"** button, or the link icon in the floating toolbar → "What do you want to link to?". Destination types: Url, Page, Anchor, Download and Email. Opening behaviour: "New window" or "Same window". To remove a link: "Unlink".

## The Inspector ("Style")

When you select an element and open "Style", you'll see different sections depending on the element type:

- **Settings** — classes and ID.
- **Visibility** — hide on mobile, tablet, small desktop or large desktop, plus opacity.
- **Padding** and **Margin** (with "Link values together").
- **Border** and **Border radius**.
- **Typography** — font family, size, weight, style, color, background, line height, letter spacing, transform and text align.
- **Background** — color or image and gradient.
- **Shadow** — add and adjust.
- **Size** — width, height, max width and min height.
- **Layout** — display, direction, wrap, justify, align and gap.
- **Position** — static, relative, absolute, fixed or sticky, with their offsets and z-index.
- **Effects** — rotate, blur, transition, cursor and overflow.

With nothing selected, the Inspector says "Nothing selected. Click any element on the left to select it." Above the Inspector you'll see the element breadcrumb, letting you click up a level.

The 74 Yammbo blocks add their own controls to the Inspector, and their labels aren't translated — you'll see things like "Title", "Theme" or "Submit button" even if the rest of your interface is in Spanish.

## Next step

Organise your content across multiple pages with [Site pages](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/site-pages/).

en.title: The editor, screen map
en.description: What each panel of the Yammbo Web editor does — the sidebar, the canvas and the bottom toolbar — so you know your way around before touching anything.
en.body:
The editor lives at `/editor/{id}`. It has three zones: a sidebar on the left, the canvas with your site in the centre, and a bottom action toolbar.

## Left sidebar

Top to bottom:

- **← Dashboard** — goes back to the dashboard.
- **Elements** — the blocks you can insert. See [Elements and blocks](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/elements-and-blocks/).
- **Layout** — containers, rows and columns.
- **Style** — opens the **Inspector**, where you adjust the styling of the selected element. See [Text, images and styles](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/text-images-and-styles/).
- **Pages** — manage the site's pages. See [Site pages](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/site-pages/).
- **Settings** — opens "Project settings": publishing, forms, leads and export. See [Publish your site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/publish-your-site/).
- **Code** — custom CSS and JavaScript (paid plans).
- **History** — a list of changes since you opened the site.

## The canvas

In the centre you see your site taking shape. Click any element to select it; right-click gives you a menu with cut, copy, paste, delete, duplicate and move.

## Bottom toolbar

Left to right: **Undo**, **Redo**, the device selector (mobile portrait, tablet portrait, small desktop, large desktop), **Design check**, **Preview** and **Save**.

## Next step

Start adding content with [Elements and blocks](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/elements-and-blocks/).

en.title: Troubleshooting
en.description: Every known message and issue in Yammbo Web, what causes it and what to do — account, AI, editing, publishing, domain, forms and export.
en.body:
## Account and access

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| The verification code never arrives | Spam filter, or the code already expired (30 minutes) | Check spam and Promotions; use the resend link on "Verify your email". If nothing arrives, write to support@yammbo.com |
| "The email or password you entered is incorrect." / "Too Many Attempts." | Wrong details, or a one-minute lockout after 5 failed attempts | Wait a minute, or use "Forgot your password?" |
| Signing in with Google or Twitter: "An account with this email address already exists…" | You'd already signed up before with that email and a password | Enter your account's password and click "Connect"; the two accounts get linked |
| I see the app (or some buttons) in English | Yammbo Web's default language is English; it follows your browser or your account setting. Some labels don't have a translation yet | Account settings → Location and language → Language → pick your language → Save. See [Your account](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/your-account/) |

## Creating a site

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "The name has already been taken." | Your project's name is **unique across all of Yammbo Web**, not just your account | Pick a different name, for example adding your city: "Tacos El Norte Monterrey" |
| I closed the window while an AI site was generating and it never showed up | The project is created once your browser receives the full result; if you close before that, it isn't saved | Don't close the window until you see "Site created with AI". Note: that generation already used up your monthly quota even if you never see the result |
| Fewer pages came out than I asked for, or "Multi-page sites require an active subscription." | Free doesn't allow multiple pages; paid plans silently trim the request down to your plan's page limit | Change plans, or create the missing pages by hand under "Pages" |

## AI in the editor

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| An AI button is greyed out, locked, or opens "Join the PROs" | AI (text and images) is a paid-plan feature only | Subscribe at `/pricing` |
| "You have used all the AI tokens included in your plan this month…" | Monthly token quota used up; a full site uses around 44,000 | Wait until the 1st, or switch to a plan with more allowance |
| You've used this month's full-site generations (5, 15 or 40 depending on your plan) | Monthly generation quota used up | Wait until the 1st, or switch to a plan with more allowance. Meanwhile, "Edit section with AI" is still available if you have tokens left |
| AI generation never finishes, or the dialog goes back to the form without showing any notice | A one-off generation failure, generation took more than 30 minutes, or you've already used this month's generations | Wait a few minutes and try again. A one-page home takes about 2-3 minutes; a multi-page site takes longer. If it keeps happening, email support@yammbo.com |
| "This section could not be replaced." / "AI response could not be parsed. Please try again." | The AI returned a response that couldn't be parsed | Try again. If the section ends up broken, use "Undo" |
| 429 error when generating sections | 20-requests-per-minute limit | Wait a minute before trying again |

## Editor and saving

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| The image won't upload: "This file type is not allowed" | The file extension is blocked | Upload JPG, PNG, WebP or SVG |
| "You have exhausted your allowed space of…" | Your plan's total storage is used up | Delete some files or upgrade your plan |
| The logo in the AI dialog won't upload | It's over 20 MB, the only limit that applies to that specific field | Reduce the image size |
| I saved, but the published site doesn't change | Unsaved changes don't publish; also, the published site is cached for 60 seconds | Click "Save", wait a minute, and reload |
| I lost changes when I closed the editor | There's no autosave and no warning when leaving with unsaved changes | Get into the habit of clicking "Save" often — the button is enabled whenever there's something unsaved |
| I can't delete a page | The `index` page, and the only page left on a site, can't be deleted | Empty its content instead of deleting it |
| "A page with this name already exists." | Duplicate page name | Use a different name |

## Publishing

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "Has alcanzado el límite de sitios publicados de tu plan…" (shown in Spanish regardless of interface language) | Only **1 site can be published at a time**, on any plan, including Pro | Unpublish the other site and publish this one |
| Opening my site's link asks me to sign in | The site **isn't published**: only its owner, signed in, can see it | Settings → Publishing → "Publish" |

## Custom domain

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| The domain never finishes connecting | Could be DNS, the `www` vs. no-`www` variant, or your domain provider | Write to **support@yammbo.com** with your domain and where it's registered; we'll walk you through it. See [Custom domain](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/custom-domain/) |

## Forms

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Form messages aren't reaching my inbox | The email notification can fail, or go to a different address than you expect | Check the **"Leads"** tab: every submission is saved there, whether or not the email arrives |
| The form doesn't work on a site exported as a ZIP or via FTP | Outside Yammbo Web, the form's internal placeholder never gets replaced with a real address | Use your own form service on your hosting, or keep the site published on Yammbo |
| 429 error when submitting a form | 10-submissions-per-minute limit | Wait a minute |

## Export

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "To download your site as a zip file upgrade your plan." | ZIP is a Standard and Pro feature | Switch to Standard or Pro |
| "To export your site via FTP or as a .zip file upgrade your plan." | FTP is Pro only | Switch to Pro |

## Other

This usually happens if you had an editor tab open from before a platform update. Force-reload with **Ctrl+Shift+R**.

| Message or symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| My site shows "Sitio no disponible" with a blurred background | This only happens for businesses that also use **Yammbo Agent**: the account is paused or has a pending payment. The site hasn't been deleted | Settle the account; the site comes back as it was. Use the contact or chat shown in the notice itself |

## If none of this solves your case

Write to **support@yammbo.com** telling us what you expected to happen and, if you can, the exact message you saw.

en.title: Your account
en.description: Profile details, password, active sessions, why the interface can show up in English, and how — and with what caveats — to delete your account.
en.body:
Open **"Account settings"** from your avatar menu, top right (that's also where "Dashboard", "Billing" if you have a subscription, and "Dark mode" / "Light mode" live).

## Details and security

- **"Account details"**: First name, Last name and Profile image.
- **"Password"**: Current password, New password and Confirm password.
- **"Two factor authentication" (2FA)**.
- **"Active sessions"**: a list of your open sessions, with a "Logout other sessions" button.

## Interface language

Under **"Location and language"** → "Date, time and language" you choose your **"Language"** (Español or English), your country and your timezone.

Yammbo Web's effective default language is English, so a new account can start in English even if your browser is set to a different language. If you'd rather use a different one, go to Account settings → Location and language → Language → pick your language → Save, and sign back in. A few labels — for example "Write with AI", "Edit with AI", or the Yammbo blocks' labels — stay in English either way, because they don't have a translation yet.

## Dark or light mode

Switch it from your avatar menu, with "Dark mode" or "Light mode".

## Deleting your account

Under **"Delete account"** → "Danger zone": "Your account will be deleted immediately and permanently. Once deleted, accounts can not be restored."

Deleting your account doesn't delete your projects with it, and if you had a site published, it stays online. Unpublish it before deleting your account (Publish › unpublish), because you won't be able to afterwards — see [Publish your site](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/publish-your-site/).

## Next step

If something isn't working the way you expected, check [Troubleshooting](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/web/troubleshooting/).

en.title: AI assistant
en.description: Connect an AI provider with your own key so it replies using your business data. Providers, model, instructions and common errors.
en.body: The AI assistant replies to your customers in its own words, using the data you filled in under [My business](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/my-business/). To use it you connect an AI provider with **your own key**, write how you want it to reply, and Yammbot creates an assistant rule. ## 1. Choose a provider From **menú › Inteligencia artificial** (menu › Artificial intelligence), choose the provider whose AI will write the replies: | Provider | What it's like | |---|---| | **Groq** | Free tier, no card: around 1000 requests a day and 30 per minute per model. Very fast. | | **Google Gemini** | Free tier, no card, with a daily request limit per model. On the free tier, Google may use your messages to improve its products. | | **Mistral AI** | Free mode, no card, with usage and rate limits. | | **OpenRouter** | Free models (ending in `:free`) cost nothing: 50 requests a day and 20 per minute. Which free models are available changes often. | | **Cerebras** | Trial with $5 of credit for 30 days; asks you to add a card. Pay-as-you-go after that. | | **OpenAI** | Pay-as-you-go: you need to add credit first. | | **Anthropic (Claude)** | Pay-as-you-go. You need to add credit first. | | **DeepSeek** | Pay-as-you-go and very cheap. You need to top up credit before using it. | | **Together** | Pay-as-you-go, with open models. You need to add credit first. | | **xAI (Grok)** | Pay-as-you-go. You need to add credit first. | | **Personalizado** (Custom) | Any OpenAI-compatible service: you set the base URL, the key and the model yourself. | The ones with a free tier don't ask for a card, but they limit how many messages you can send per day and per minute. The paid ones charge by usage. ## 2. Get and paste your key The key (API key) is like a password the provider gives you so Yammbot can use your account. Creating it is free and it's **stored only on your phone** — never on our servers or in the cloud backup. 1. Open the provider's website. 2. Create your account or sign in with the one you have. 3. Create a new key and copy it. Some sites only show it once. 4. Come back to Yammbot and paste it in the key field. ## 3. Choose the model The model is the specific AI that writes the reply. If you're not sure which one to pick, leave the recommended one — it's at the top of the list. You can also type the exact name of a model that isn't on the list. ## 4. Assistant instructions In **«Cómo debe responder»** (How it should reply) you write the tone and limits for the assistant. They apply to all AI rules and you can use [variables](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/creating-rules/#variables) like `%business_name%`. Yammbot always adds, even if you don't write it, that it **must not invent prices or data** and that it should say a person will answer if it doesn't know something. You can restore the suggested text whenever you want. Other assistant settings: - **Memoria de la conversación** (Conversation memory) — how many previous messages of that chat it remembers (off, 3, 6 — recommended — or 10 messages), up to 24 hours, to understand questions like "and in red?". - **Temperatura** (Temperature) — how much the reply style varies: **Precisa** (Precise) sticks to your data and answers almost the same way every time, **Equilibrada** (Balanced) is a middle ground, **Creativa** (Creative) varies more. For customer service, use Precise or Balanced. - **Largo de la respuesta** (Reply length) — Short, Normal or Long (the maximum tokens it can use). - **Prefijo** (Prefix) — fixed text added before every reply, for example "Virtual assistant:". ## 5. Create the assistant rule For the AI to reply, you need an **assistant rule**. You can choose its scope: - **Todos** (Any) — replies to any message using the My business data. Keep it last in your rule list so your other rules reply first. - With another match type, it only replies to messages that match its triggers. Fallback replies for the assistant rule: - **Respuesta si hay un error** (Reply if there's an error) — sent if the AI fails (no credit, no internet, provider limit). Empty sends nothing. - **Respuesta si se infringe una política** (Reply if a policy is violated) — sent if the AI refuses to reply because of its content rules. Empty sends nothing. ## Testing the connection In Ajustes (Settings), the **«Probar conexión»** (Test connection) button sends a test message to your provider and shows you the response, to confirm the key and model work before using them with customers. ## Common errors | Message | What it means | What to do | |---|---|---| | The key is wrong or doesn't have permission | The provider rejected your key | Copy it again from the provider's website | | That model doesn't exist or your account can't use it | The chosen model isn't available for your account | Pick another one from the list | | Your account has no credit | The provider requires credit and you don't have any | Add credit on the provider's website or choose one with a free tier | | You've hit your provider's limit for now | You went over the daily or per-minute request limit | Wait a few minutes or try tomorrow | | The provider has a problem right now | An outage or incident on the provider's side | Try again later | | The provider took too long to respond | The request timed out | Try again | | The provider blocked the reply under its content policies | The customer's message or the reply violated the provider's rules | Review the assistant's instructions; use the fallback reply | | The provider replied, but with no text | Empty response from the provider | Try another model | | The service address isn't valid | Custom provider only: the base URL is malformed | Check it matches the format the provider asks for (for example ending in `/v1`) | | Missing the key, model or service address | Incomplete configuration | Fill in all three fields before saving | | No connection | The phone has no internet | Check the phone's connection | Replies given by the AI are counted separately in Results, in the breakdown at bot.yammbo.com/panel/resultados. The app only shows replies sent today.

en.title: App messages and what they mean
en.description: A table with every reason Yammbot's history shows when a rule doesn't reply, and what to do about each one.
en.body:
When a message arrives, the **Historial** (History) tab logs what happened, including the exact reason if no reply was sent. This table collects the most common reasons.

## General reasons

| Message | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| No rule matches | None of your rules had a trigger that matched that message | Review your rules' [matching](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/creating-rules/#matching-when-the-rule-fires), or add an [AI](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ai-assistant/) rule with "Any" scope to cover what doesn't match anything |
| The rule doesn't send a reply | The rule matched but is deliberately set to "No reply" | Normal if you use it only for a submenu or an alert |
| The reply was empty | The rule was about to reply but the text ended up empty | Check the reply text in the rule's editor |
| Rule paused in this chat | That rule already fired recently in this chat and its pause hasn't ended | Expected behavior of the [pause](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/creating-rules/#delays); lower the pause time if you want it to reply more often |
| The rule repeated too soon | It fired several times in a row in a short time and Yammbot stopped it | Check "Prevent repeated rules" in Settings |
| Replies paused | The general auto-reply switch is off | Turn it on from Home or Settings |
| Channel disabled | That app's channel isn't active in Yammbot | Enable it under [Channel apps](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/channel-apps-and-accounts/) |
| Ignored chat | That chat is on your ignore list | See [Ignored chats](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ignored-chats/) |
| Matches "Don't reply if" | The message matched an exclusion condition you set | Check "Don't reply if" in Settings |
| Didn't reply because you're handling this chat | The chat is paused by [takeover](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/when-you-reply-yourself/) | Wait for the pause to end or tap "Resume" in Paused chats |
| Groups aren't allowed | A group message reached a rule that only replies to individual chats | Change "Recipients" to Groups or Both — see [Apps, accounts and groups](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/channel-apps-and-accounts/#groups) |
| The notification doesn't allow a reply | The notification arrived without a "Reply" button, so Yammbot can't answer it | Check whether the chat is open on screen, or whether that app isn't supported yet |
| Canceled before sending | Another rule canceled this reply before it went out ("Cancel pending replies") | Expected behavior if you set that option |
| No connection | The phone had no internet at that moment | Check the phone's connection |
| Timed out | Sending took too long | Usually resolves itself; check your connection if it keeps happening |
| Couldn't send | The reply failed to send through the messaging app | Check that app is working normally |

## Account and access reasons

| Message | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Message reached an account Yammbot doesn't reply on | The message arrived on an account you didn't enable | Check which accounts are enabled in [Channel apps](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/channel-apps-and-accounts/) |
| [Rule] matches, but didn't reply: missing [detail] | The rule needs a My business detail you haven't filled in yet | Fill in that detail under [My business](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/my-business/) |
| The notification no longer allowed a reply (the chat was opened or deleted) | You opened or deleted the chat before Yammbot could reply | Expected behavior; Yammbot needs the notification to stay active |
| No access: your free month ended | Your trial ended and you don't have an active plan | Choose a plan under [Plan, payments and billing](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/plan-and-billing/) |
| No access: this phone already used the free month with another account | This phone doesn't get a free month for the new account | Choose a plan to keep using Yammbot |
| No access: not signed in or your plan isn't active | You're not signed in to the app, or your plan isn't active | Sign in and check your plan |
| No access: it's been more than 7 days without being able to check your plan | The phone has gone over a week without connecting to check your access | Connect the phone to the internet |

## AI errors

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| AI error | Groups together any failure from the AI provider while generating the reply |

See the full table of AI errors, with cause and fix, in [AI assistant › Common errors](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ai-assistant/#common-errors).

## Webhook error

| Message | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Webhook error | Your server didn't respond, returned an error, or returned something that isn't valid JSON | Check the URL, user and password in [Webhook](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/webhook/), and that your server is reachable |

## Yammbo POS error

| Message | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| POS error | Yammbo POS didn't respond or the connection is no longer valid | Test the connection with **Probar conexión** (Test connection) on the Yammbo POS screen; if the code is no longer valid, pair again from your Yammbo POS panel — see [Connecting Yammbo POS](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/yammbo-pos/) |

## Where you see these reasons

In the **Historial** (History) tab, every entry shows "Reason: [text]" when no reply was sent. You can also filter the history by channel or show only priority alerts.

en.title: Channel apps, accounts and duplicate apps
en.description: Which messaging apps Yammbot recognizes, how to pick specific accounts, and how it works with duplicate apps, work profiles and groups.
en.body:
## Channel apps

In **menú › Apps de cada canal** (menu › Channel apps) you choose which app you use for each channel (WhatsApp, Messenger, Telegram). Yammbot replies on the apps you check there.

### Which apps work

Any app that shows each message in a notification with a **Reply** button. Yammbot replies from that notification, without opening the app. This includes variants like WhatsApp Business, Telegram X, Plus Messenger, Messenger Lite or a similar app: enable it or add it to its channel just like the main app.

Web versions opened in a browser (Telegram Web, WhatsApp Web) almost never let you reply from the notification. For Yammbot to reply, use the phone app.

### If you don't have any app installed

If no app for a channel is installed, Yammbot lets you know: you'll be able to choose that channel from Home once you install it.

## Accounts

If you use several accounts of the same app (for example, two WhatsApp Business numbers with duplicate apps), Yammbot can reply on all of them or only on some:

- If the app doesn't show the account in its notifications, Yammbot replies on all of your accounts of that app.
- If you want to pick, use the [Notification inspector](#notification-inspector) to measure how your notifications arrive, then turn on **«Responder en esta cuenta»** (Reply in this account) for the ones you want.
- Messages where the app doesn't say the account show up as **«Sin cuenta identificada»** (Unidentified account) — with duplicate apps, that's usually the main app.

Yammbot identifies the account from the Android profile, your name in the app, or the notification text, depending on what that app shows.

In a rule's editor, **«Solo en estas cuentas»** (Only on these accounts) limits that rule to the accounts Yammbot already recognized — if none are checked, it replies on all of them.

## Duplicate apps and work profiles

In **Ajustes › Perfiles de trabajo y apps duplicadas** (Settings › Work profiles and duplicate apps), turn this on so Yammbot treats messages from each profile or duplicate app as separate chats (for example, regular WhatsApp and a cloned WhatsApp in a work profile). It's useful if you use cloned apps to keep a personal number separate from a business one on the same phone.

## Groups

Yammbot's plans include replying in groups. Every new rule starts with the **Destinatarios por defecto** (default recipients) from Ajustes (Settings); change them on the rule to **Grupos** (Groups) or **Ambos** (Both) if you also (or only) want to reply in groups. If a rule without that change receives a group message, it's logged as **«Los grupos no están permitidos»** (Groups aren't allowed).

## Notification inspector

**Apps de cada canal › Inspector de notificaciones** (Channel apps › Notification inspector) records what your apps' notifications look like: Android profile, names, fields and buttons. It never stores the message text, only how many characters it has. It turns itself off after 30 minutes and keeps the last 50 notifications. It helps you understand why Yammbot does (or doesn't) identify a specific account, and you can export the log to send to support if needed.

en.title: Cloud backup
en.description: What Yammbot's cloud backup saves, what it doesn't include, how to restore it and how to move to a new phone.
en.body:
Cloud backup saves your setup to your Yammbo account, so you don't lose it if you switch phones or reinstall the app.

## Turning it on

In **Ajustes › Copia en la nube** (Settings › Cloud backup), turn on **«Guardar mi configuración en mi cuenta»** (Save my setup to my account). From there you can tap **«Guardar ahora»** (Save now) whenever you want, or let it save on its own.

## What it includes

- Your rules.
- Your variables.
- Your reply settings.
- The data from [My business](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/my-business/).

## What it does NOT include

Your AI provider keys, your webhook passwords and the app's PIN are **not** saved in the cloud backup. For your webhook headers, only their names are copied, never their values. You'll have to set them up again by hand after restoring.

## How it's stored

The backup is saved **encrypted** in your account. Yammbot keeps the **10 most recent backups**; saving a new one drops the oldest. If you have no rules or variables to save, no backup is created.

## Restoring a backup

Restoring is always done **from the app**, never from the web panel:

1. Open Yammbot on the phone where you want to restore and sign in with your account.
2. Go to **Ajustes › Copia en la nube › Recuperar una copia** (Settings › Cloud backup › Restore a backup).
3. Pick the backup you want to recover.

Restoring replaces your current rules and variables. Your AI keys and the app lock don't change when you restore.

If you sign in with an account that has a saved backup and your phone is empty, Yammbot suggests it right away: "You have a backup of your setup from [date]. Want to restore it?", with the option to **«Empezar de cero»** (start fresh) if you'd rather not use it.

## Switching phones

1. On your old phone, sign out (or save a manual backup first).
2. Install Yammbot on the new phone (see [Download and install Yammbot](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/download-and-install/)).
3. Sign in with your account.
4. Restore the cloud backup when the app suggests it.

## Viewing them from the web panel

On **bot.yammbo.com/panel/copias** you see the list of saved backups (date, phone, app version, number of rules and variables) — never the content. It's for reference only; restoring always has to happen from the app. See [Your account's web panel](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/web-panel/).

en.title: Creating and editing rules
en.description: Match types, replies, multiple replies, delays, submenus and variables — how Yammbot's rule editor works.
en.body: A rule says **what message to expect** and **what to reply**. For example: if someone writes "hours", reply "We're open from 9 to 6". You create and edit them from the **Reglas** tab (Rules). ## Creating a rule From **Reglas › Nueva regla** (Rules › New rule) you can choose: - **Desde plantilla** (From template) — ready-to-use rules (greeting, hours, prices…). See [My business](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/my-business/#general-rule-templates). - **En blanco** (Blank) — you set up the expected message and the reply yourself. Every rule has two required sections: **Coincidencia** (Matching) and **Respuesta** (Reply); the rest are optional: **Destinatarios y canales** (Recipients and channels), **Condiciones** (Conditions), **Opciones** (Options) and **Submenú** (Submenu). ## Matching: when the rule fires In **Disparadores** (Triggers) you write which messages activate the rule, using one of these types: | Type | How it works | Example | |---|---|---| | **Exacta** (Exact) | Replies if the message equals one of the phrases, case-insensitive. Several phrases separated by commas. | `hours` | | **Contiene** (Contains) | Replies if the message contains any of the words or phrases, ignoring case and accents. | "hours" matches "what are your hours?" | | **Patrón** (Pattern) | Wildcards: `*` is any text, `?` is one character and `\|` means "or". | `hi*`, `*price*`, `hi\|hello` | | **Similitud** (Similarity) | Replies if the message is close enough to one of the phrases. Phrases separated by `//`. The minimum closeness is set in Ajustes (Settings), «Umbral de similitud» (Similarity threshold). | — | | **Regex** | Case-insensitive regular expression. Captured groups are used in the reply as `%capturing_group_1%`. | `^hi`, `order\s+(\d+)` | | **Todos** (Any) | Replies to any message. Doesn't need triggers. | — | | **Bienvenida** (Welcome) | Replies to the first message of each chat since the bot was turned on. Doesn't need triggers. | — | You can also write **«No responder si»** (Don't reply if), globally in Ajustes (Settings): if the message matches that condition, nothing is sent. Useful for skipping thank-you messages or messages with links. ## Reply How the reply is generated: - **Texto** (Text) — the text you write in Reply. - **IA** (AI) — an [AI assistant](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ai-assistant/) replies. - **Webhook** — your own server replies. See [Webhook](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/webhook/). - **No enviar respuesta** (No reply) — the rule matches but doesn't answer; useful for alerts or for jumping to another rule. ### Multiple replies You can add more than one reply to a rule and choose how they're sent: - **Todas** (All) — sends them one after another. - **Al azar** (Random) — sends one picked at random. - **Rotar** (Rotate) — sends a different one each time, in order. ### Delays - **Retardo de respuesta** (Reply delay) — a short wait before replying, so it feels written by a person. Set to «Como en Ajustes» (Like in Settings) to use the global delay (instant, natural 3-8 s, or relaxed 15-40 s). - **Retardo entre respuestas** (Delay between replies) — the wait between each reply, when a rule sends more than one. - **Pausa** (Pause) — stops the same rule from firing again in the same chat for a time you choose (0 = no pause). ## Submenu A submenu chains sub-rules that are only evaluated if **this** rule was the last one to fire in that chat. For example: a "Menu" rule offers options, and sub-rules "1", "2" and "3" only reply if the customer just received that menu. - **Vigencia del submenú** (Submenu validity) — how long the sub-rules are expected after this rule fires (0 = no limit). - **Después, ir a** (Then, go to) — instead of (or besides) replying, jumps to another rule's menu without sending that rule's own reply. ## Recipients, channels and conditions A rule can be limited to: - Specific **Canales** (channels) and **Cuentas** (accounts) (if none are checked, it replies on all of them). - Specific **contacts**, or ignoring certain contacts within that rule. - **Destinatarios** (Recipients): individuals, groups or both. - **Horario** (Schedule) — see [Schedules](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/schedules/). - **Requisitos** (Phone requirements) — driving mode, charging, Do Not Disturb, screen off, silent mode. - **Probabilidad** (Probability) — firing only a percentage of the time. - **Alerta prioritaria** (Priority alert) — shows its own notification when the rule fires, for example if the customer asks for a human. ## Variables A variable gets replaced by its real value when the reply is sent. They're grouped into: - **Mi negocio** (My business) — the data you filled in under [My business](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/my-business/). - **Del mensaje** (From the message) — data from the message that arrived, like the sender's name. - **Del contexto** (From context) — for example, the groups captured by a Regex rule. - **Fecha y hora** (Date and time). - **Aleatorias** (Random). - **Personalizadas** (Custom) — the ones you create in **Ajustes › Variables** (Settings › Variables), for text you repeat across several rules (a promo, your shipping terms, a link). You edit them once and every rule using them updates. | Variable | Replaced with | |---|---| | `%business_name%` | Your business name | | `%business_description%` | Your business description | | `%business_hours%` | Your hours | | `%business_address%` | Your address | | `%business_phone%` | Your phone number | | `%business_website%` | Your website | | `%business_delivery%` | How you handle deliveries | | `%business_payments%` | Your payment methods | | `%business_products%` | Your products and prices | | `%first_name%` | The name of whoever wrote to you | | `%capturing_group_1%` | The first group captured by a Regex rule | To insert one, tap **«Insertar variable»** (Insert variable) in the reply field and pick it from the list. Save the rule and test it in Probar (Test), from Inicio (Home). The simulated chat shows the real reply and delay, without sending anything. ## Duplicate, reorder, export - **Drag** a rule in the list to change its order — Yammbot applies the first one that matches. - **Duplicate** creates a copy ("Rule (copy)") to build on. - **Export rules** / **Import rules** saves or loads all your rules in a file, handy for moving your setup to another phone without using [cloud backup](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/cloud-backup/).

en.title: Download and install Yammbot
en.description: How to download the Yammbot APK outside Google Play, install it, pass Play Protect and turn on notification access.
en.body:
Yammbot installs from an APK file, outside Google Play. It takes a few minutes and you do it from the phone where you want it to reply.

## 1. Download the file

Go to [bot.yammbo.com/descargar](https://bot.yammbo.com/descargar) from your Android browser and tap **«Descargar APK»** (Download APK). If the browser warns that the file could be harmful, confirm you want to download it anyway — that's normal for any APK that doesn't come from Google Play.

The download page also shows the file's **SHA-256** checksum, in case you want to verify it from a computer.

## 2. Allow the install

Open the downloaded file. If Android asks, turn on **"Allow from this source"** (or **"Install unknown apps"**) for your browser and go back to continue installing.

## 3. If Google Play Protect appears

Play Protect may warn that the app wasn't downloaded from Google Play. Tap **"More details"** and then **"Install anyway"**. You don't need to turn off Play Protect.

## 4. Sign in to your account

Create your account or sign in with the one you already have. Your free month starts the first time you sign in **from the app** — not when you register on the website. See [Getting started](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/getting-started/) for the rest of the initial walkthrough.

## 5. Turn on notification access

The app takes you straight to that Android setting. It's the permission that lets it read a new message and reply from the notification.

Android blocks this permission for apps installed outside Google Play. To unlock it:

1. Open the app's **info screen** (or Settings › Apps › Yammbot).
2. Tap the **⋮** menu in the top corner.
3. Choose **"Allow restricted settings"** and confirm.
4. Go back to the app and turn on notification access again.

## 6. Remove the battery restriction

Choose **"Unrestricted"** so Android doesn't close Yammbot in the background. If your phone is a Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo or Samsung, also check the manufacturer guide in [Not replying](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/not-replying/#manufacturers).

## Updates

Since Yammbot isn't on Google Play, updates don't arrive on their own: the app itself tells you when there's a new version (**Acerca de › «Buscar actualización»** (About › "Check for update")). Download the new APK and install it over the one you have, without uninstalling — your rules and settings are kept.

## Next step

Continue with [Getting started](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/getting-started/) to set up your account, permissions and the first walkthrough inside the app.

en.title: Frequently asked questions
en.description: Quick answers about privacy, battery, channels, pricing and your Yammbot account.
en.body:
## Does Yammbot read my conversations?

It only sees the text that arrives in a new message's notification and compares it to your rules, on the phone itself. If you set up a [webhook](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/webhook/), an [AI](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ai-assistant/) or [Yammbo POS](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/yammbo-pos/), that message's text is sent to that service to generate the reply. Yammbo doesn't store your conversations on its servers. See [What is Yammbot?](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/what-is-yammbot/#privacy-what-happens-to-your-messages).

## Does it drain a lot of battery?

No. Yammbot only works when a message notification arrives; the rest of the time it's idle. What it does need is for battery to be set to "Unrestricted" so Android doesn't close it while it waits for those notifications.

## Does it work if I have the chat open on screen?

Not at that moment: the messaging app doesn't show a notification while the chat is open, so Yammbot never finds out about the message. It will reply to the next message once you close the chat.

## Does Yammbot reply on Instagram?

Not yet. For now it replies on WhatsApp, WhatsApp Business, Messenger and Telegram. Instagram is **coming soon**.

## Does Yammbot change my WhatsApp number or use the WhatsApp Business API?

No. It replies from your own WhatsApp, using the "Reply" button on the notification, just like you would by hand.

## Can I use it with several accounts or duplicate apps?

Yes. See [Channel apps, accounts and duplicate apps](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/channel-apps-and-accounts/) to pick which accounts each rule replies on and how it works with work profiles.

## Does it reply in groups?

Yes, if you set it up: every new rule starts with the **Destinatarios por defecto** (default recipients) from Ajustes (Settings); change them on the rule to **Grupos** (Groups) or **Ambos** (Both). See [Groups](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/channel-apps-and-accounts/#groups).

## How much does it cost and when does the free month start?

$4.99 USD a month or $39.99 USD a year, with a 30-day free trial, no card, that starts the first time you sign in **from the app**. See [Plan, payments, canceling and refunds](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/plan-and-billing/).

## My phone didn't get a free month, why?

The free month is one per account and one per phone. If that phone already used it with another account, the new account starts without a free month. If you think that's a mistake, write to soporte@yammbo.com.

## What happens to my rules if I switch phones?

Turn on [cloud backup](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/cloud-backup/) before switching phones: when you sign in with your account on the new one, Yammbot offers to restore it. You can also save your rules to a file with **Exportar reglas** (Export rules), in the **Reglas** (Rules) tab.

## How many phones can I connect to my account?

There's no documented limit on the number of phones. You can see and manage all of them at [bot.yammbo.com/panel/dispositivos](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/web-panel/#dispositivos-devices-paneldispositivos).

## How do I cancel or delete my account?

See [Plan, payments, canceling and refunds](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/plan-and-billing/) to cancel, and [Your account's web panel](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/web-panel/#deleting-your-account) to delete the account.

## Where do I ask for help if none of this answers my question?

Write to **soporte@yammbo.com** telling us your phone model and what you expected to happen. Before writing, check [Not replying](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/not-replying/) and [App messages and what they mean](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/app-messages/) — they solve most cases.

en.title: Getting started: account, free month and permissions
en.description: Yammbot's initial walkthrough step by step — channels, permissions and what to expect the first time you open the app.
en.body:
The Yammbot app and the bot.yammbo.com panel are in Spanish. Button names are shown exactly as they appear, with an English translation in brackets.

The first time you open Yammbot, the app walks you through a short tour (**«Paso X de Y»** ("Step X of Y")) that leaves everything ready to reply. You can replay it any time from Ajustes (Settings), **«Repetir el asistente de permisos»** (Replay the permissions wizard).

## 1. Welcome

The welcome screen sums up the idea: Yammbot replies for you on WhatsApp, Messenger and Telegram with simple rules, and you can pause it whenever you want.

## 2. Your account and the free month

You create your account or sign in with the one you already have. This part matters:

**Your free month (30 days, no card) starts the first time you sign in from the app** — not when you register on the website. If you created the account on bot.yammbo.com and haven't opened the app yet, your free month hasn't started.

It's one free month per account and per phone: if that phone already used the free month with another account, the new account doesn't get one. If you think that's a mistake, write to support.

## 3. Choose your channels

Check the messaging apps where you want Yammbot to reply: one or several. If you don't have any supported app installed, you can pick a channel later from **Inicio** (Home).

## 4. How Yammbot uses your notifications

Before asking for the permission, the app explains:

- It reads the notifications of the messaging apps you enable, and only those.
- It only uses them to reply according to the rules you create.
- It doesn't send your messages to anyone else, except the webhook or AI you configure yourself (or Yammbo POS, if you connect it).

## 5. Notification access

This is Yammbot's core permission: without it, it can't see that a new message arrived or reply to it. Find **Yammbot** in the list Android opens and turn it on. If the switch looks locked, see [Download and install Yammbot](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/download-and-install/#5-turn-on-notification-access).

## 6. Unrestricted battery

This keeps the system from stopping Yammbot while the phone is idle, so replies go out on time. In the app list, find Yammbot and choose **"Don't optimize"** or **"Unrestricted"**.

## 7. Yammbot's notifications

Allow the app's own notifications: it tells you when it replies, when something fails, or when a customer needs attention (for example, with a priority alert).

## 8. Last step

With notifications, battery and internet ready, you choose which apps you want Yammbot to reply in and finish the walkthrough.

## After the walkthrough

With the app installed and permissions on, continue with:

- [My business and setting up by business type](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/my-business/) to create your first rules in a minute.
- [Creating and editing rules](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/creating-rules/) if you'd rather build them yourself from scratch.
- [Testing your rules](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/testing-rules/) before using them with real customers.

en.title: Ignored chats
en.description: How to make Yammbot never reply in certain chats, either globally or inside one specific rule.
en.body:
There are chats where you don't want Yammbot to ever reply — your family, say, or a supplier. That's what ignored chats are for.

## Ignoring someone globally

In **Ajustes › Ignorar a** (Settings › Ignore), type the names as they appear in the chat, separated by commas (for example: `Mom, Family group`). Yammbot never replies to them, on any rule.

The same way, **«Responder solo a»** (Reply only to) does the opposite: if you fill it in, Yammbot only replies to those names and no one else.

## Ignoring a contact inside a rule

You can also limit this to a single rule, in its recipients section: **«Ignorar estos contactos»** (Ignore these contacts) makes that particular rule never reply to the names you type there, even if the rest of your rules still do.

## The phrase to ignore a chat

Instead of writing the name ahead of time, you can ignore a chat on the fly by typing a phrase inside that chat (see [When you reply yourself](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/when-you-reply-yourself/#messages-to-pause-or-reactivate-a-chat-by-hand)). The chat stays marked as ignored until you type the reactivation phrase.

## What you see in the history

An ignored chat shows up in the [history](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/app-messages/) with the reason **«Chat ignorado»** (Ignored chat) — that's how you confirm Yammbot did see the message but chose not to reply on purpose.

en.title: My business and setting up by business type
en.description: Fill in your business profile and create your first rules in a minute, picked for your type of business.
en.body: **menú › Mi negocio** (menu › My business) is where you save your business details once. Rule templates and the [AI assistant](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ai-assistant/) use them to reply, so filling it in well improves all your answers. ## What you'll fill in - **Datos básicos** (Basic details) — business name, type of business, what you do and for whom in a sentence or two. - **Contacto** (Contact) — phone, address, website. - **Qué ofreces** (What you offer) — your products or services with prices, one per line. - **Cómo atiendes** (How you serve customers) — shipping, home delivery, in-store, online or by appointment. - **Preguntas frecuentes** (Frequently asked questions) — the ones you get a lot and how you answer them. There's a maximum number of questions; if you hit it, delete one to add another. - **Otros datos** (Other details) — policies, warranties, promotions and anything else the assistant should know. You can leave blank anything you don't want to share. The profile shows how many of those fields you've already completed (for example, "6 of 10 fields complete"). What you write here is used by the AI assistant to reply, and by rule templates to fill in your answers automatically with [variables](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/creating-rules/#variables) like %business_hours% or %business_products%. ## Choosing your type of business Picking a business type changes the examples and suggested questions in your profile — it doesn't create or delete rules by itself. The available types are: | Business type | Meant for | |---|---| | Store or selling products | Physical and online stores, catalog, shipping | | Beauty | Salon, barbershop, nails, spa | | Health and clinics | Doctors, dentists, psychologists, physiotherapy, vets | | Technical services and repairs | Phones, computers, appliances, cars, plumbing | | Professional services | Lawyers, accountants, agencies, consultants | | Education and courses | Schools, academies, private lessons, online courses | | Real estate | Selling and renting houses, apartments and units | | Hotel and tourism | Hotels, hostels, cabins, tours | | Gym and sports | Gyms, yoga or dance studios, sports clubs | | Restaurant or food | Restaurants, cafés, takeout and delivery | | Other | Any other business. Start with the basic rules | ## Set up by business type (1-minute setup) From **menú › Configura en 1 minuto** (menu › 1-minute setup), or from the **Crear reglas para mi tipo de negocio** (Create rules for my business type) button in My business: 1. **Pick your business type.** Yammbot suggests the rules that businesses like yours use most. 2. **Review the rules that will be created.** They're added before any rule that replies to everything (like the AI assistant), so they don't get shadowed. None of your existing rules are deleted. 3. **Fill in any missing details.** A rule that's missing a detail is created unchecked, with a field to type it in right there; filling it in checks the rule. It isn't created at all if you don't fill it in. 4. **Uncheck the ones you don't want and tap Crear (Create).** Rules that match a name you already have aren't duplicated. Once created, review and test them in [Testing your rules](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/testing-rules/) before using them with customers. ## General rule templates Besides the rules by business type, **Nueva regla › Desde plantilla** (New rule › From template) has ready-made templates for any business: greeting, hours, location, prices and catalog, payment methods, shipping and delivery, talk to a person, away reply, after hours, welcome new customers, thank you, AI assistant and selling with Yammbo POS. Pick one, review the text and save it — you can change anything afterward.

en.title: Yammbot isn't replying: troubleshooting guide
en.description: The full checklist for when Yammbot doesn't reply, the "Not working" assistant inside the app, and settings by manufacturer.
en.body:
If Yammbot isn't replying, check these points **in this order** — the problem is almost always one of the first few.

## 1. Your plan is active

Open your [panel](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/web-panel/) or **Planes** (Plans) inside the app and confirm your free month or subscription is still active. See [Plan, payments, canceling and refunds](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/plan-and-billing/).

## 2. Notification access is still on

Android sometimes revokes it on its own, especially after a system update. Go to Android Settings › Notifications › Notification access and confirm Yammbot is still turned on. If the switch looks greyed out or says **"Restricted setting"**, see the note below.

## 3. Battery is set to "Unrestricted"

If Android optimizes Yammbot's battery, it can close it in the background and stop it from replying. Go to Android Settings › Apps › Yammbot › Battery and choose **"Unrestricted"**.

## 4. The channel's notifications aren't muted

If you muted notifications for that chat or for the whole app, Yammbot never finds out a message arrived. Check that WhatsApp, Messenger or Telegram have their notifications on, and that chat in particular isn't muted.

## 5. The message matches a rule and is within its schedule

Check your rule's matching (see [Creating and editing rules](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/creating-rules/#matching-when-the-rule-fires)) and whether it has a [schedule](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/schedules/) set. Test it in **Inicio › Probar** (Home › Test) with the exact text of the message.

## 6. The chat isn't paused because you took it over

If you replied to that chat by hand or tapped **«Atiendo yo»** (I've got this), Yammbot pauses it for a while. Check **menú › Chats en pausa** (menu › Paused chats) — see [When you reply yourself](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/when-you-reply-yourself/).

## 7. The chat isn't on your ignore list

See [Ignored chats](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ignored-chats/).

## 8. If you use webhook or AI, they're set up correctly

Check the URL, user and password of the [webhook](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/webhook/), or the key and model of the [AI assistant](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/ai-assistant/#common-errors). AI has a **Probar conexión** (Test connection) button under menú › Inteligencia artificial (menu › Artificial intelligence); webhook has no test button of its own, so check it by firing a real rule or with the simulated chat in Probar (Test).

## The "Not working" assistant inside the app

Yammbot has its own assistant, **menú › No funciona** (menu › Not working), that checks these same points step by step. It's the fastest way to diagnose things without going through the list by hand.

## Common cases

### "Restricted setting" (the switch looks greyed out)

Android blocks notification access for apps installed outside Google Play until you allow it by hand:

1. Open Yammbot's **app info screen**.
2. Tap the **⋮** menu in the top corner.
3. Choose **"Allow restricted settings"** and confirm.
4. Go back to Yammbot and turn on notification access again.

### Manufacturers

Some manufacturers close background apps with their own settings, on top of Android's:

- **Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo, Samsung** — besides setting battery to "Unrestricted", look in the phone's settings for something like **"Autostart"** or **"App suspension"** and exclude Yammbot.

### The chat is open on screen

When you have a conversation open, the messaging app doesn't show a notification — and without a notification, Yammbot never finds out about the message. It will reply to the next message once you close the chat.

### Android removed notification access

Android sometimes revokes this permission on its own, usually after a system update. Turn it back on under Android Settings › Notifications › Notification access.

### Your phone didn't get a free month

The free month is one per account and one per phone. If that phone already used it with another account, the new one doesn't get a free month. If you think that's a mistake, write to support.

Write to **soporte@yammbo.com** telling us your phone model and which rule you expected to reply. In the meantime, check the table of [app messages and what they mean](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/app-messages/) — it usually says exactly why it didn't reply.

en.title: PIN lock, widget, quick settings and updates
en.description: Protect Yammbot with a PIN, turn it on or off without opening the app from the widget or quick settings, and how updates arrive.
en.body: ## App lock In **Ajustes › Seguridad › Bloqueo de la app** (Settings › Security › App lock) you can require Yammbot to unlock when opened, so no one else can change your rules from your phone. There are three options: - **Sin bloqueo** (None) — anyone with your phone can open Yammbot. - **PIN de 5 dígitos** (PIN) — a 5-digit code specific to Yammbot, independent from your phone's own lock. - **Huella o bloqueo del sistema** (System lock) — your fingerprint, your face or your phone's screen lock, if your model supports it. ### Creating or changing your PIN Choose a 5-digit PIN and repeat it to confirm. It will be asked every time you open Yammbot. You can change it later from **Ajustes › Cambiar PIN** (Settings › Change PIN). The PIN isn't included in the cloud backup: it's a local setting on that phone. If you forget it, the app offers no way to recover it. ## Home screen widget Yammbot has a home screen widget that lets you see and change the state of auto-replies (on or paused) without opening the app. Add it like any other widget: long-press your home screen, choose **Widgets** and look for Yammbot. ## Quick settings Yammbot also adds a tile to Android's **quick settings** (the panel you pull down from the top). Edit your quick settings to add it, and you'll be able to turn auto-replies on or off with a tap, just like Wi-Fi or airplane mode. ## App updates Since Yammbot is installed outside Google Play, updates don't arrive on their own: - The app itself tells you when a new version is available. - You can check yourself in **Acerca de › «Buscar actualización»** (About › "Check for update"). - If there's a new one, it downloads inside the app; install it over the one you have, without uninstalling, to keep your rules and settings. See the full first-install walkthrough in [Download and install Yammbot](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/download-and-install/).

en.title: Plan, payments, canceling and refunds
en.description: Yammbot pricing, how the free month works, how to pay, cancel, what happens if a charge fails and how to ask for a refund.
en.body:
## Pricing

| Plan | Price |
|---|---|
| Monthly | $4.99 USD a month |
| Yearly | $39.99 USD a year |

Both plans include exactly the same thing: all channels, unlimited rules, AI, webhooks, groups, schedules and the Yammbo POS connection. See current pricing at [bot.yammbo.com/precios](https://bot.yammbo.com/precios).

## The free month

Every new account gets **30 days free, no card required**. Two things matter here:

- **It starts the first time you sign in from the app** — not when you register on the website. If you signed up on bot.yammbo.com but haven't opened the app yet, your free month hasn't started.
- It's **one free month per account and per phone**. If that phone already used the free month with another account, the new account doesn't get one. If you think that's a mistake, write to support.

Once the free month ends, Yammbot stops replying until you pick a plan. Nothing is charged automatically, because a card is never requested during the trial.

## How to pay

You pay with a credit or debit card through **Stripe**, from the app or from your panel at **bot.yammbo.com/panel/plan**. Prices are in US dollars. Yammbo never sees or stores your card details.

## Managing payment and invoices

Under **Plan y facturación** (Plan and billing) in the panel, the **«Gestionar pago y facturas»** (Manage payment and invoices) button opens Stripe's secure portal, where you can:

- Change your card.
- Download your receipts.
- Cancel the subscription.

In the app, the equivalent button is just called **«Gestionar pago»** (Manage payment).

## How to cancel

1. Go to your panel, under **Plan y facturación** (Plan and billing) (or in the app, under **Planes** (Plans)).
2. Tap **«Gestionar pago y facturas»** (Manage payment and invoices) in the panel, or **«Gestionar pago»** (Manage payment) in the app.
3. Choose to cancel the subscription and confirm.

You can cancel any time, no calls or commitment. When you cancel:

- The subscription won't renew and you won't be charged again.
- You keep access until the end of the period you already paid for — your panel shows the exact date.
- Once that period ends, Yammbot stops replying. Your rules stay on your phone and, if you had it turned on, in your [cloud backup](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/cloud-backup/).
- You can subscribe again whenever you want.

## If a charge fails

If a renewal charge fails, Stripe retries it and you keep access for a **3-day grace period**. If it isn't resolved by then, access stops until you update your payment method under «Gestionar pago y facturas» (Manage payment and invoices).

## Refunds

Yammbo reviews every refund request case by case — for example, a mistaken charge, a duplicate charge, or a service issue that couldn't be fixed. Keep in mind you can try every feature for a month before paying.

To request one, write to **soporte@yammbo.com** from your account's email, with the charge date and the reason. If approved, the refund goes back to the same card through Stripe; how long it takes to show up depends on your bank. This doesn't limit any refund or withdrawal rights your country's law gives you.

Stripe emails you a receipt with every payment, and you can always download them from «Gestionar pago y facturas» (Manage payment and invoices) in your panel.

en.title: Results
en.description: What numbers Yammbot sends every day, what you see in the app and in the web panel, and how to turn it off.
en.body:
Yammbot counts what it does for you. In the app you only see replies sent today; the full breakdown lives on your web panel, adding up all your phones if you use more than one.

## What it counts

- **Messages received.**
- **Replies sent.**
- **Fallos** (Failed) (a rule matched but the reply couldn't be sent).
- **AI replies.**
- **Yammbo POS replies.**
- **Times you handled it yourself** (chats paused by [takeover](https://help.yammbo.com/docs/en/yammbot/when-you-reply-yourself/)).
- **Chats atendidos** (Chats handled).
- **Time saved** — calculated as 1 minute per reply sent.

On the web panel, all broken down by day, by channel and by phone.

Once a day, the app sends only these counts — never the content of your messages or your customers'. You can turn the upload off in Ajustes (Settings) if you'd rather not share it; in that case you won't see results on the web panel, but Yammbot keeps replying all the same.

## In the app

**Inicio** (Home) shows a summary of the day (replies sent today) and shortcuts. For the full detail, Yammbot opens your browser and takes you to the web panel.

## In the web panel

On **bot.yammbo.com/panel/resultados** you pick the period (7, 30 or 90 days) and see:
